newsitem.title: USA: American Air, pilots in last-ditch talks.
newsitem.headline: American Air, pilots in last-ditch talks.

text.p: American Airlines, a unit of AMR Corp, and its pilots union on Monday opened last-ditch contract talks with the aim of making "a deal" to avert a threatened nationwide strike.
If no agreement is reached by midnight Friday, the Allied Pilots Association pledged to walk off their jobs, shutting down the operations of the nation's second-largest carrier.
American Airlines President Donald Carty told reporters just before the talks started that his negotiators were in Washington "to make a deal."
Carty told reporters the aim of both the carrier and the union was a strong American Airlines, adding "all we need is a commercial agreement" to reach that ideal.
The pilots president, James Sovich, said separately "we're here to get a deal also."
One key issue in the dispute is pay - the Fort Worth, Texas-based carrier's 9,000 pilots want an increase of 11.5 percent over four years. American has offered five percent.
Another issue is American's plan to add jets to its commuter line, American Eagle. American Airlines pilots fear the company will use the lower-paid American Eagle pilots to take jet work from them.

The talks moved to Washington, with the National Mediation Board participating, after the rejection by rank-and-file pilots of an agreement reached by its negotiators and the failure of reopened talks to resolve the differences.

On Friday, members of the Senate Commerce committee urged President Clinton to help mediate the dispute, but the White House indicated it would not intervene unless asked by both sides. But it said just before the talks began, that it would follow the deliberations "carefully between now and Friday."
